channel_name: The Prof G Show · Scott Galloway
video_title: What Happens If Democrats Win the Midterms? — With Fareed Zakaria
gist: On midterm election day, Fareed Zakaria tells Scott Galloway that a record 45% independent electorate and collapsing Trump gains among Hispanics and young voters could make the US the first major break in global right-wing populism, with the Iran war (the most unpopular in US history, tied to inflation) a key driver. He argues allies like Canada and India are 'buying insurance' against America (e.g., every new US iPhone now made in India, French jets for India), proposes flattening ~7,000 tariff rates into a 5-7% import tax, and joins Galloway in condemning Musk's Starlink throttling in Ukraine.

themes.theme: Midterm dynamics: the Trump coalition unwinds

insights.claim: Zakaria says 45% of the American electorate now identifies as independent, the highest ever, creating an unusually large pool of malleable swing voters beneath a narrow polarized base on each side.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Elections are more contestable than the polarization narrative implies; larger swings are possible.
insights.quote: 45% of the American electorate is now independents uh highest number ever.

insights.claim: Zakaria says Trump's 2024 gains among Hispanics have collapsed (down close to 20 points), and gains among young voters and Black men have also reversed, returning young voters to an Obama-2008-like split.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Erosion of the 2024 coalition raises odds of a Democratic wave.
insights.quote: he's down close to 20 points from where he was in 24.

insights.claim: Only 38 House seats were competitive due to gerrymandering, but Zakaria argues gerrymanders that spread safe Republican margins thinner (e.g., from +20 to +8-9) can backfire in a D+12 wave.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Wave elections can flip more seats than models built on static gerrymanders assume.

insights.claim: Zakaria says Trump's approval in the 36-37% range makes him basically the most unpopular president in American history, with only Nixon near his resignation comparable.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Low approval will invite a crowded Democratic 2028 field and weakens administration leverage.

insights.claim: Zakaria argues a US blue wave could be the first major global break in the 10-year wave of right-wing populism, which he frames as a backlash against 30 years of technological, economic and cultural acceleration offering a politics of nostalgia.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: A US reversal could signal peaking populism globally, shifting policy-risk assumptions.

insights.claim: Zakaria says populist policies have not delivered: Britain is worse off after Brexit, manufacturing has not returned to the US, and the US has not decoupled from China.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Delivery failures on reshoring and decoupling undermine the political base for those policies.
insights.quote: manufacturing is not back in the United States.

insights.claim: Zakaria notes Lula in Brazil is the only president to lose the first round and win the second, shifting 10 million votes in three weeks.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Late electoral swings can be very large.

insights.claim: Zakaria argues corruption and executive overreach only began to resonate once tied to pocketbook issues (linking corruption to grocery affordability) and to visible ICE raids.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Affordability is the transmission channel turning governance issues into votes.

insights.claim: Zakaria warns Democrats must convert anti-Trump sentiment into an energetic centrism rather than far-left identity politics, citing polling that a majority of Democrats want the party in the center.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Whether Democrats move center or left shapes post-midterm policy risk.

themes.theme: Iran war, inflation, and executive power

insights.claim: Zakaria calls the Iran war the most unpopular war in American history and the first in the modern era unpopular from day one, because its rationale is unclear and it is directly tied to inflation.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: War-driven inflation is a direct electoral liability for the administration.
insights.quote: The Iran War has been unpopular from day one, the most unpopular war in American history.

insights.claim: Zakaria says the war appears aimed at regime change that failed in the first three days, six months after a bombing campaign that set back Iran's nuclear program likely by years, and six months in it has not ended.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Prolonged war sustains energy-driven inflation pressure.

insights.claim: Zakaria argues Democrats can use the Iran war to rein in executive power, which the founders intended to be subordinate to Congress but has become king-like, especially given Supreme Court rulings.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: A Democratic Congress may push war-powers and executive-authority constraints.

insights.claim: Zakaria argues allies burned by two Trump elections will 'buy insurance' through diversification even under a future Democratic president, so the pre-Trump order cannot be fully restored.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Hedging away from US dependence is structural; expect lasting trade and defense diversification.
insights.quote: once you sew that level of mistrust that doubt that sense that we need a bit of insurance it's hard to see how you how you get

insights.claim: Canada under Mark Carney is making deals with the EU, China and India to regain leverage after the integrated North American auto industry (parts crossing borders up to 15 times) became a vulnerability.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Canadian trade diversification erodes US leverage and North American supply-chain integration.

insights.claim: India, which gets about 80% of its weaponry from Russia, placed its big order this year for French fighter planes rather than American, and will wean off Russia more slowly than planned because elite views of the US have changed.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: US defense exporters are losing a major potential market share shift in India.

insights.claim: Zakaria says every new iPhone sold in America is now made in India, up from zero three years ago via Tata, and 25% of smartphones are made in India, because only India has the scale to offset China.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: India is the only scaled China+1 manufacturing alternative; supports India manufacturing exposure.
insights.quote: Today, every new iPhone in America is made in India. 25% of all smartphones are made in India.

insights.claim: Australians believe the Trump administration is slow-walking the AUKUS submarine deliveries, leaving them having angered China with nothing in return.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: US credibility on defense commitments is eroding in the Indo-Pacific.

insights.claim: Galloway frames US alliances as a 'controlling interest' of roughly 60-70% of world GDP among democracies, which the US is voluntarily diluting to a minority position.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Loss of alliance 'voting control' could weaken dollar and US policy leverage over time.

themes.theme: Policy playbook for a Democratic Congress

insights.claim: Zakaria proposes Democrats regularize the roughly 7,000 tariff rates and exemptions, some seemingly bought through corruption, into a flat 5-7% import consumption tax, since the Treasury is now addicted to tariff revenue.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: A flat low tariff regime would lower effective import costs while keeping revenue; reduces exemption-lobbying.
insights.quote: the Treasury is at this point addicted to the tariffs.

insights.claim: Galloway proposes a Democratic Congress pass a resolution matching or exceeding Europe's Ukraine support with US technology and dare Trump to veto it; Zakaria agrees Ukraine is the central struggle of the post-1945 no-annexation norm.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Ukraine aid votes are likely early signaling moves after a Democratic win.

insights.claim: Zakaria recommends long-term locked-in commitments such as a 15-year trade agreement with Canada and tech partnerships with India, ideally with Republican support as NAFTA had.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Durable trade agreements would reduce policy volatility for North American supply chains.

themes.theme: Musk, Starlink and the limits of tech power

insights.claim: Galloway argues Elon Musk throttling Starlink during Ukraine's war amounts to treason against the West, and that idolization of wealthy innovators provides cover for it.
insights.speaker: Scott Galloway
insights.so_what: Dependence on privately controlled satellite infrastructure is a geopolitical risk.
insights.quote: I think Elon Musk is a traitor to the West.

insights.claim: Musk's public appeal to Mukesh Ambani to allow Starlink in India backfired, rallying nationalists behind Reliance's Jio satellite effort; Indians feared Ukraine-style dependence on a Trump-and-Musk-controlled system in a Pakistan conflict.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Starlink's India expansion faces nationalist resistance favoring Reliance Jio.

insights.claim: Zakaria argues DOGE's $2 trillion cut target was impossible because the federal government is 'an insurance company with an army' whose spending is benefits, not administrative staff.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Meaningful fiscal cuts require benefit changes, not headcount cuts.
insights.quote: the federal government is basically an insurance company with an army.
